mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending power and corporate earnings visibility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as recessionary expectations dominate market pricing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, signaling active monetary tightening, higher borrowing costs pressure corporate valuations and consumer spending, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained corporate earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105.0 signals manufacturing sector contraction, reducing corporate output capacity and earnings visibility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 105.0 (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises (measured over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 > 11200), strong GDP growth sustains corporate earnings momentum, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as market participants price in continued economic expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 11200 (measured over 3-year rolling window).
